deposits.notes: The paper links this single PDF on saved-v1 pp. 1, 6, 7, 12 and 69. The preview URL and its ordinary dl=1 download both returned HTTP 200. Downloaded 5,410,503 bytes in memory and inspected the 135-page PDF, its contents, page text and links; no embedded files or repository/data links. The live PDF is dated October 2026, so it is newer than the saved July 2026 paper. Sections: student experiment instruments (pp. 2-104), essay-quality assessment instrument (pp. 105-122), and learning readings (pp. 123-135). Calibration examples with suggested scores are grader-training materials, not identifiable participant outcome records. No participant roster, assigned-arm variable, participant outcome scores or essay corpus. No explicit license located.

Saved-v1 p. 79, Figure B1, links this illustrative automation conversation. Public HTML contains the conversation in embedded JSON; is_public=true, accessible without login. Parsed linear_conversation has 9 nodes, including 4 user/assistant messages. rows_checked counts serialized conversation nodes, NOT participants or essays; columns_checked lists message-object keys, NOT study variables. No study participant ID, randomized-assignment field, outcome grades, inclusion flags, control-arm records or link to the analysis sample. The paper situates these examples among treated ChatGPT users (pp. 75, 80), but that context is not an assignment variable in the transcript. Contains an AI-produced draft and a student-pasted edited essay in a word-count request. The 567-word figure is ChatGPT's reply, not a verified study outcome. One attachment, blockchain.pdf (79,164 bytes), is listed in public message metadata; its downloadability was not verified and it is the reading stimulus. n_files refers to attachment metadata, not the HTML page. The thread identifier is not a participant ID. These selected texts cannot support group means, SDs, SEs, analysis counts or representative between-arm diversity. No license found.

Named only in the latest arXiv v2, p. 1: AEARCTR-0015806. Title, investigators and two-session design match S1. The public record says, under Data Publication, 'Is public data available?' followed by 'No'. It exposes one public Analysis Plan attachment, labeled PAP: https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/versions/317677/docs/version/document (HTTP 200; 32-page PDF; 443,115 bytes; filename confirmed by Content-Disposition). The PAP is dated April 2025 and contains design/analysis plans and reading materials, with no participant dataset, embedded files, external data links or data-sharing promise. Program Files and Reports & Other Materials have no public attachments listed. The page also says some trial information is unavailable to the public and offers Request Information; no request was made and no hidden information was accessed. This does not establish that participant data are available on request. The registry record and PAP themselves are public. Registry DOI https://doi.org/10.1257/rct.15806-1.1 returned HTTP 200 and redirected to /trials/15806/history/317678. License not stated.

deposits.notes: Discovered through the arXiv landing page's TeX Source link while checking the DataCite preprint match. Public gzip/tar archive downloaded and inspected entirely in memory (10222728 bytes); 205 regular files enumerated. Listed files are capped at 50 and prioritize the CSV. results/kv_store.csv (28571 bytes) was parsed in full: 412 rows with unique statistic keys, not participant rows. Columns are key, value, timestamp, label. Values are aggregate sample counts, descriptive summaries, effect sizes and other manuscript constants. No participant IDs, participant assignment vector, individual outcome scores, inclusion/exclusion flags, or complete essay corpus. The text flag is true only because manuscript/figure files include selected verbatim student prompts and three illustrative open-ended narratives; these are unlinked to participant records or arms. The archive contains manuscript TeX, bibliography, figures and aggregate table fragments; 00README.json is an arXiv compilation manifest, not participant data or analysis code. This is the version corresponding to the saved PDF and form; its aggregate n_both_sessions is 204. It does not identify the participants behind the conflicting Session One linguistic N values or provide complete exclusion accounting.

notes: Checked 10 October 2026 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without authentication, web search, account creation or access requests. Read all 209,724 characters of the saved markdown in contiguous chunks, including Appendices A-C (93 PDF pages); verified availability statements and link annotations against PyMuPDF text. Quotes normalize PDF line wrapping and discretionary line-break hyphenation only. The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are empty. No public participant-level analysis dataset was found. Public partial evidence consists of aggregate CSVs in arXiv source archives and two selected student chat transcripts; survey instruments and the PAP are also public. None supplies the complete participant sample linked to randomized arm, outcomes and texts. Therefore no missing item in final.open_items can be computed or settled from the public data: the v1 Table 5 versus A5 count discrepancy and complete exclusion accounting remain unresolved. The two measure-code open items require Atlas coding decisions, not data. The requested new participant-based means, SDs, SEs and representative diversity measures cannot be computed from these materials. The latest arXiv landing page and PDF returned HTTP 200 and identify v2 dated 4 October 2026; v2 adds an AEA registration and changes sample-related statistics. Latest-version evidence is explicitly labeled and does not replace the saved v1. DataCite returns the preprint, not a dataset, and its relatedIdentifiers/relatedItems are empty. All four specified repository APIs were searched by full title and first-author name; OSF's required title-filter endpoint is limited to title matches. The two initial Zenodo searches returned HTTP 400 because anonymous page size is capped at 25; both were retried successfully at size=25. No matching OSF, Harvard Dataverse or Zenodo deposit was found, so there was no repository file inventory to fetch there. No GitHub repository is named. All five unique HTTP(S) links embedded in the saved PDF were requested: the Dropbox and two ChatGPT URLs are recorded as deposits; https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08849v1 returned HTTP 200; the unrelated bibliographic correction https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2518204122 returned HTTP 403 with a bot-check page, and was not pursued. The unversioned landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08849 also returned HTTP 200. Email links were not contacted. PDFs, archives and data were inspected in memory; only this requested report is written.
